title: Su-25SM / SM3 Frogfoot

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: The Su-25SM is a modernised version of the armoured Su-25 attack plane, and the SM3 is its latest step. The old ASP-17 gunsight gives way to a head-up display and a colour multifunction display, both part of the PrNK-25SM navigation and attack system; the SM3 adds the SOLO-25 targeting system. The stick and the twin throttle are those of the Su-25, so this guide follows the DCS Su-25 and adds the SM's new displays. The SM stick has one extra unlabelled button whose function is not public.

panels.name: Head-up display of the PrNK-25SM
panels.text: The SM replaces the old ASP-17 gunsight with a real head-up display, a glass screen in front of the pilot's eyes that shows flight numbers and aiming marks.
panels.context: It is part of the new PrNK-25SM navigation and attack system, which works out where weapons will hit.

controls.name: Head-up display
controls.text: The glass screen in front of the pilot's eyes. It shows speed, height, heading and the aiming marks for the gun, rockets and bombs.
controls.context: The pilot looks through it during an attack run and keeps both eyes outside.

controls.name: HUD control panel
controls.text: A small panel with the settings of the head-up display, such as its brightness and what it shows.
controls.context: The exact switches of this panel are not described in the sources JoyPro uses.

panels.name: Colour multifunction display
panels.text: A colour screen in the instrument panel with buttons around its edge. It shows navigation, weapons and, on the SM3, the SOLO-25 targeting system.
panels.context: It brings a map and the weapon status onto one screen, which the original Su-25 did not have.

controls.name: Colour MFD
controls.text: The colour screen itself. It can show a moving map, the route, the weapons and the targeting pictures.
controls.context: The pilot switches between these pages during the mission.

controls.name: MFD bezel keys
controls.text: Buttons around the edge of the screen. Each one picks the word printed next to it on the screen.
controls.context: The same button does different things on different pages.

controls.name: Navigation data entry panel
controls.text: A keypad where the pilot types navigation data, for example the points of the route (waypoints, points on the planned route the plane can steer to).
controls.context: The navigation system then guides the pilot along these points to the target and home.
